entries.name: Correspondent banking
entries.definition: Arrangements in which one bank provides services such as payments and account access to another bank, often across borders.

entries.name: Cosmetic dermatology
entries.definition: The branch of dermatology that improves the appearance of skin, hair and nails, for example with fillers, lasers and peels.

entries.name: COSO framework
entries.definition: A framework published by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission for designing and assessing internal control and enterprise risk management.

entries.name: Cost accounting
entries.definition: The part of accounting that records and analyses the costs of making goods or providing services so managers can control and price them.

entries.name: Cost estimating
entries.definition: Predicting what a project, product or job will cost before it is done.

entries.name: Cost to serve
entries.definition: A way of working out how much it costs a business to serve each customer, product or channel, counting activities such as delivery, handling and support.

entries.name: CoStar Real Estate Manager
entries.definition: A CoStar Group cloud software product for managing leases, property portfolios and real-estate costs.

entries.name: Counterparty risk
entries.definition: The risk that the other party to a financial contract will fail to meet its obligations.

entries.name: CPython
entries.definition: The reference implementation of the Python language, written in C.

entries.name: Crane signaling
entries.definition: Guiding a crane operator during a lift with standard hand signals or radio calls.

entries.name: Craniofacial surgery
entries.definition: The surgical specialty that repairs and reshapes the skull, face and jaws, including congenital differences such as cleft lip and palate.

entries.name: Create React App
entries.definition: A command-line tool from Facebook that sets up a new React web application with a ready-made build configuration.

entries.name: CreateJS
entries.definition: A suite of JavaScript libraries for building interactive HTML5 canvas content, including EaselJS, TweenJS, SoundJS and PreloadJS.

entries.name: Creative arts therapy
entries.definition: Using art, music, dance or drama in a therapeutic setting to support people's emotional and mental health.

entries.name: Creative problem-solving
entries.definition: Finding original solutions to problems by generating and testing new ideas.

entries.name: Credit risk analysis
entries.definition: Assessing how likely a borrower is to fail to repay and how much a lender could lose if that happens.

entries.name: Creo Elements/Pro
entries.definition: A parametric 3D computer-aided design package from PTC, formerly known as Pro/ENGINEER.

entries.name: Crestron
entries.definition: Control and automation systems for audio-visual equipment, lighting, shades and building technology, made by Crestron Electronics.

entries.name: Crestron programming
entries.definition: Writing the control programs that run Crestron audio-visual and automation systems.

entries.name: Crime analysis
entries.definition: Studying crime reports and data to find patterns and help police prevent and solve crimes.

entries.name: Crime mapping
entries.definition: Plotting crime data on maps to find hotspots and patterns that guide policing.

entries.name: Crime scene investigation
entries.definition: Securing, documenting and collecting physical evidence at the place where a crime happened.

entries.name: Criminal intelligence
entries.definition: Information about criminals, their networks and activities that police gather and analyse to prevent and investigate crime.

entries.name: Critical path method
entries.definition: A project scheduling technique that finds the longest chain of dependent tasks, which sets the shortest possible project duration.

entries.name: Critical reflection
entries.definition: Examining your own assumptions, actions and experience in order to learn from them and improve practice.

entries.name: Critical test results management
entries.definition: The process of promptly telling the responsible clinician about dangerous laboratory or imaging results and recording that it was done.

entries.name: Crop farming
entries.definition: Growing crops such as grains, vegetables and fruit, including preparing soil, planting, tending and harvesting.

entries.name: Cross-domain solutions
entries.definition: Security systems that let information move between networks of different classification levels under strict controlled rules.

entries.name: Cross-platform app development
entries.definition: Building applications that run on more than one operating system or device type from a shared codebase.

entries.name: Cross product
entries.definition: An operation on two three-dimensional vectors that gives a third vector perpendicular to both.

entries.name: CRUD
entries.definition: The four basic operations of persistent data storage: create, read, update and delete.

entries.name: CryEngine
entries.definition: A game engine from Crytek for building 3D games and real-time visualisations.

entries.name: Cryptocurrency
entries.definition: Digital money secured by cryptography and usually run on decentralised blockchain networks, such as Bitcoin.

entries.name: CU-SeeMe
entries.definition: An early internet videoconferencing program developed at Cornell University.

entries.name: Cucumber
entries.definition: A behaviour-driven development tool that runs plain-language Gherkin specifications as automated tests.

entries.name: Cucumber.js
entries.definition: The JavaScript implementation of Cucumber, which runs plain-language Gherkin specifications as automated tests.

entries.name: Cultural sensitivity
entries.definition: Recognising and respecting differences in cultural background, beliefs and customs when dealing with people.

entries.name: Culture transformation
entries.definition: Changing the shared values, habits and behaviours of an organisation so that it can reach a new goal.

entries.name: CUnit
entries.definition: A lightweight unit testing framework for writing, administering and running tests in C.

entries.name: Cured-in-place pipe
entries.definition: A trenchless method of repairing a damaged pipe by inserting a resin-soaked liner that is hardened in place to form a new pipe inside the old one.
